then.text: Your verse is going round the market already. Somebody's put it on a tea towel.
Máire sent you? With a new limerick? Then stand up on that crate and give it to the crowd. Then you face me.

You recite: 'A young trainer who came to King John's / Brought a team made of ducks and of swans. / They hissed at the gate, / And a guard yelled, "Ye're late!" / And they guard it themselves now with wands.'
Ha! Wands! Go on, Ruairí, top that!
The Milk Market gives you a round of applause and a free scone. Back to Máire at the Poet's Rest.

else.text: Market day's for verse and cheese. Come back when you've a limerick of your own. Máire at the Poet's Rest will set you right.

milk_cheese.text: Farmhouse cheese from Clare and Limerick and Cork. This one's washed in cider. This one's washed in sea water. This one, I'd rather not say.
Saturday's the big day. The whole county's in here by nine. By ten there's no parking from here to Ennis.

milk_baker.text: Brown soda bread, white soda farls, barmbrack, and a tart that'll make your granny jealous.
The market's been here since 1852. The canopy's newer. The rain is the original.
